rows.value: Equilateral N = p*R*s/(2*sqrt(3)) = 562166 N at s 2.04 m. p*R*s/2 = 973701 N is the two-way force.
rows.issue: The first filing sized the equilateral grid at the two-way force. Yield, Euler, local and Perry were low by sqrt(3). Global was not. The sleeve total at equilibrium, with the radius held, does not depend on s.
rows.consequence: Masses in the first report are the two-way masses. This card replaces them for the equilateral grid.
rows.next: 022b rescales with C*N^2/r for a sleeve and with the tube area for a braze.

rows.value: 1470 MPa compression, ASTM D695, Torayca T700S with 250 F epoxy, normalized to 60 percent fiber volume. Tensile 2550 MPa on the same sheet is not used. Density 1550 kg/m3 is the 011b quasi-isotropic value.
rows.issue: The lightest joint is this wrap: 0.015 kg per end and 31.0 kg at 562.2 kN. The fiber and the coupon exist today. A wound transition on an SiC tube does not.
rows.consequence: The mass is a sizing, not a qualified joint. Using the tensile allowable would understate it.
rows.next: A compression coupon of the wrap, bonded to SiC, at the bond length this card sizes.

rows.value: 28.9 MPa at 25 C, ASTM D1002, LOCTITE EA 9394 AERO, phosphoric-acid anodized 2024-T3 bare aluminum, cured 5 days at 25 C. 22.7 MPa at -55 C and 20.7 MPa at 82 C. Peel is low.
rows.issue: The paste exists today. The adherend in the coupon is aluminum, not SiC. The bond at 562.2 kN on the 011b radius is 25.0 mm. It uses 28.9 MPa with no temperature knockdown and no peel length.
rows.consequence: Every bonded sleeve and the wrap carry this transfer. A lower shear lengthens the bond and raises the mass in proportion.
rows.next: Lap shear of EA 9394 on the SiC surface that would actually be bonded, at the service temperature.

rows.value: AMS 4911 annealed Ti-6Al-4V, minimum yield 827 MPa, minimum ultimate 896 MPa, density 4.43 g/cm3. The pin shear is 0.6 times that yield, derived here, not a handbook shear.
rows.issue: The sheet exists today. At 562.2 kN the sleeve is 0.075 kg per end and 157.7 kg, 0.70 times the 225.5 kg allowance. Frozen least SF is 1.232 by the film. Re-optimised least SF is 1.431 at k 0.2 and 1.995 at k 0.4.
rows.consequence: At the equilateral force the titanium sleeve fits inside the 5 percent allowance. The first filing's 473.1 kg was the two-way force.

rows.value: Carpenter Invar 36, annealed bars and strip, yield 276 MPa, ultimate 448 MPa, density 8.05 g/cm3, linear CTE 1.3 µm/m-C near 93 C.
rows.issue: The alloy exists today and is the expansion match. At 562.2 kN the sleeve is 0.410 kg per end and 858.6 kg, 3.81 times the allowance. Frozen least SF is 1.054, global. Re-optimised least SF is 1.245 at k 0.2 and 1.616 at k 0.4.
rows.consequence: Invar now closes. It remains several times the 5 percent allowance. The CTE advantage is not scored as a stress.
rows.next: None, unless a higher allowable or a shorter bonded detail is sourced.

rows.value: 25 MPa compressive shear, the low end of 25-30 MPa, Cusil-ABA on monolithic SiC/Mo and SiC/Kovar. Singh and Asthana, J. Materials Engineering and Performance, 2020, doi 10.1007/s11665-020-04934-3.
rows.issue: The shear pair is a lab result. At 562.2 kN the socket is the tube wall continued for 28.9 mm, 0.062 kg per end and 130.6 kg, 0.58 times the allowance. Frozen least SF is 1.232. A solid node is not sized. A co-sintered frame is a PROJECTION. The 342 MPa bend result failed in the ceramic and is not a shear allowable.
rows.consequence: This is the lightest metallic path, and it is not a catalog node.
rows.next: A shear measurement on the tube diameter, and a socket section if the wall cannot simply continue.

rows.value: Pin mass 0.202 kg at 562.2 kN, diameter 26.9 mm, two-wall bearing 11.9 GPa on the 0.880 mm tube.
rows.issue: The rough 0.5 kg titanium fitting was this pin at the two-way force. At 562.2 kN it is 0.202 kg and the wall still cannot bear it. The titanium sleeve is 0.075 kg.
rows.consequence: The 0.5 kg figure is not the joint mass, and it is not a usable detail on this wall.
rows.next: None. The pin is a reference, not a candidate.

rows.value: Hexoloy SA flexural strength 380 MPa. Compressive strength 3900 MPa is the allowable 011b scored. Axial stress at the filed wall is 824.7 MPa at 562.2 kN.
rows.issue: Against 3900 MPa the contact factor is 4.73. Against 380 MPa it is 0.461, and the member itself fails. This card does not replace the 011b allowable.
rows.consequence: A joint sized to the flexural coupon rejects the tube that 011b accepted.
rows.next: MAINLINE-025 owns the allowable. No change here.

rows.value: Tube density 3100 kg/m3, kept so the 5 percent regression matches 011b. Hexoloy SA sheet density is 3.15 g/cm3.
rows.issue: Substituting 3150 would raise the brazed-socket mass about 1.6 percent and would move the recovered safety factor. It was not substituted.
rows.consequence: The socket mass is slightly light relative to the sheet density. The sleeve and wrap masses do not use the ceramic density.
rows.next: None, unless the frame density is changed in a later card.
